newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - New England consolidation needed.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - New England consolidation needed.

text.p: New England electric and natural gas distribution utilities will need to consolidate to compete in an era of deregulation, Bay State Gas Co president Joel L. Singer said in an interview.
The consolidation, which is needed to control costs, will be driven by the unbundling of rates.
He said acquiring and being acquired "both make sense" for Bay State, adding: "We're looking at things," without elaborating.
"It comes down to share value," Singer said, noting the consolidation will come "about twice as fast as you predict."
He said the "glimpse of the future" provided by the residental pilot unbundling program begun last August by Bay State "says you need scale" to compete in the future.
Writing in the company's annual report, Singer said "we expect to see significant consolidation in the natural gas industry" over the next several years.
"We expect this consolidation will also include electric utilities, as deregulation in the electric industry brings similar cost pressures" to those already seen by natural gas distributors.
